title: AWS Compute Services: A Study Sheet for the SAA-C03
dek: EC2, Lambda, Elastic Beanstalk, Batch, Lightsail and Outposts, and how to tell them apart on the exam.
author: Daniel Mansfield

blocks.text: AWS groups its compute services into four types: virtual machines, serverless, orchestration and containers. This sheet covers the first three, and containers get their own lesson. The main thing to know for the exam is who manages the servers in each one.

EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) runs Linux or Windows virtual servers that you manage remotely from a browser, the command line or an API. It is infrastructure as a service, and a lot of other AWS services run on EC2 underneath.

items: You choose the operating system, storage, number of vCPUs and the CPU type: Intel, AMD or Graviton, the processor AWS designed itself
Pay as you go, or reserve instances for a set period
You can use a dedicated physical server that only your organization uses
It is elastic, so you can resize it at any time and let it scale automatically with traffic

blocks.title: Shared responsibility for EC2
items: AWS manages the data centers, hardware, host operating system and virtualization layer
You manage the guest operating system, patches, security controls and your data

blocks.text: Lambda is serverless. You upload code, a function or a whole application, and AWS runs it without you managing any servers. You only pay for the compute time you use.

items: It scales to thousands of requests in seconds and is highly available with no extra work
It supports Java, Go, Ruby, Node.js, Python and others through runtimes

blocks.text: Serverless still uses servers. AWS just manages all of them, so unlike EC2 you can never access the servers under a Lambda function.
These two don't compute anything themselves. They organize groups of EC2 instances for you, and you can still reach those instances, which is the difference from Lambda.

items: **Elastic Beanstalk** deploys your application and handles capacity, load balancing, database management, auto scaling and health monitoring. You keep full control of the instances underneath
**AWS Batch** runs batch workloads by planning, scheduling and running jobs on EC2, with no batch software or clusters for you to manage

**Amazon Lightsail** is a virtual private server for a low, predictable monthly price, with its own console separate from the main AWS console. It can also set up databases, load balancers and DNS records
**AWS Outposts** is a hybrid service. AWS delivers a fully assembled server rack to your own data center, and you plug it in to run AWS services like EC2 on premises

blocks.title: Match the phrase to the service
items: No server management, pay only for compute time, run code: Lambda
Full control of the operating system, resize and scale: EC2
Upload the app and AWS deploys it, with access to the instances: Elastic Beanstalk
Batch jobs and scheduling: AWS Batch
Run AWS in your own data center, hybrid: Outposts

blocks.text: You can't reach the servers behind Lambda, but you can reach the instances behind EC2, Batch and Beanstalk.
